as_if_always.answer: yes, by the cells; the filing does not say so in words
as_if_always.quote: Page 37 heading: 'Gross insurance contract outstanding claims provision as at 31 December 2022'. Page 36 text: 'The following tables show the estimates of cumulative incurred claims, including both claims notified and IBNR for each successive underwriting year at each reporting date, together with cumulative payments to date.' And at foot of the table: '2021 Year of account has not been presented above as the Syndicate did not participate on this year of account.'
as_if_always.cells: The 2022 gross table (p37, printed 35) carries full early-development history for 2013-2020: e.g. 2018 column 44,984 / 100,979 / 105,633 / 113,604 / 115,426 (end of year, +12, +24, +36, +48 months) and 2019 column 104,174 / 184,687 / 225,235 / 199,843, years the syndicate did not write itself (S5678's 2018 and 2019 years come in by the RITC). The 2021 filing's gross table (2021 filing p28, printed 28) has no 2018 column at all, and shows 2017 as 16,398 / 20,940 / 25,189 / 22,634 / 25,052 (paid 16,230, outstanding 8,822) against 91,445 / 135,308 / 150,628 / 145,199 / 149,880 / 149,860 in the 2022 table (paid 124,175, outstanding 25,685); 2019 shows 58,790 / 67,383 / 107,888 (outstanding 75,954) in the 2021 table against 104,174 / 184,687 / 225,235 / 199,843 (outstanding 99,161) in 2022; 2013-2016 columns are also restated upward (e.g. 2016 end-of-year 53,309 in 2021 vs 77,395 in 2022). So the acquired books' history is carried back to the underwriting-year start, and the older columns are on a restated basis, not the previous report's figures. 'Paid to date' on the 2020 column is only 4,650 against a current estimate of 123,833, so paid history is not carried back for all acquired years.

ADC', 'Reinsurance accepted' creditors 4,248 + 29,294, p32). It therefore ADDS gross claims outstanding. The OUTWARD (ceded) cover is the Gibson Re WQS (80% funds-withheld whole account quota share): it moves the reinsurers' share (274,249 at year end vs 52,444), not the gross reserves.

takeon_base_m.derived_indicative_m: about 221.885 + (221.879 - D) = about 443.8 - D, where D is gross development in 2022 on the opening book (not printed; sign unknown); this is a derivation, not a printed figure
takeon_base_m.vs_analysis_opening_reserves_gbp_m: analysis opening 221.885 equals the printed opening R exactly and contains no take-on. On the derived indicative figure the take-on base is roughly double the analysis opening (about 2.0x if D = 0). Closing 489.603 is 2.21x the opening.

1110_2022.note: The take-on is large relative to the opening book (closing gross reserves 2.2x the opening) and the RITC history is restated into the development table. Gross claims movement in the filing is confounded with the take-on: note 3 has no transfer row. A defensible take-on figure needs a source outside this filing (the S5678 RITC statement, the Hiscox ADC premium or the opening position of the acquired years), or an explicit choice to exclude the record. The gross development table's 2022 values are on a restated basis (differences in 2013-2016 columns against the 2021 filing exceed 7 percent at end of underwriting year), so a latest-less-previous mature-cohort figure cannot be built from the 2021 and 2022 filings' tables like for like; the 2022 table's own latest diagonal reconciles to the gross claims outstanding of 489,603.

1458_2024.note: The take-on is small against the opening book. Because the development table carries the acquired history as if always, the mature-cohort movement from the table (-33.258m USD, -26.56m GBP) already excludes the take-on, and only the denominator R is short by the acquired reserves. The size cannot be read off the filing: it needs the RITC statement or the RITC premium from outside the filing. The RITC counterparty and date are not given in the filing. The report's gross written premium, claims note and managing agent's report do not isolate the RITC.
